# fastqcviz <a href='https://github.com/barreiro-r/fastqc-viz/'><img src='man/figures/logo.png' align="right" height="138" width="120"/></a>

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/barreiro-r/fastqc-viz/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/barreiro-r/fastqc-viz/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/barreiro-r/fastqc-viz/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/barreiro-r/fastqc-viz)
[![lifecycle](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://www.tidyverse.org/lifecycle/#experimental)
<!-- badges: end -->

The `fastqcviz` package was developed to give [FastQC](https://github.com/s-andrews/FastQC) reports the aesthetic and functional love it deserves, transforming its insights into a more visually appealing experience without changing the core analysis. A modest re-desing update for the classic FastQC report. 

classic report: [FastQC](https://www.bioinformatics.babraham.ac.uk/projects/fastqc/good_sequence_short_fastqc.html) | ✨ `fastqcviz` report : [fastqcviz](https://html-preview.github.io/?url=https://github.com/barreiro-r/fastqc-viz/blob/example/example.html)


![before-and-after](man/figures/before-after.png)


## Installation

You can install the development version of fastqcviz from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
devtools::install_github("barreiro-r/fastqc-viz")
```

## Example

Using fastqcviz is as easy as:

```{r example, eval=FALSE}
library(fastqcviz)

create_fastqcviz_report(
  fastqc_path = "path/to/sample_fastqc/fastqc_data.txt",
  output_dir = "fastqcviz_report",
  embed_resources = TRUE)
```
